sentiment.rationale: Full-year guidance for net sales (3.5%-4.5% cc), adjusted operating income (6%-8% cc), and adjusted EPS ($2.75-$2.85) is reiterated unchanged from the original February 2026 guidance, despite a Q1 beat on revenue (5.7% cc vs. 4.0%-5.0% guided range) and a strong Q2 operating income guide (7%-10% cc). The Q1 beat is partially organic (eCommerce, advertising, marketplace) but management explicitly attributes a 250 bps headwind to higher fuel costs and notes that if elevated costs persist, 'somewhat higher retail price inflation' is expected. The unchanged full-year guidance and cautious inflation language prevent a higher score, but the Q2 acceleration and strong operational momentum (e.g., general merchandise share gains, advertising growth) justify a mildly positive score.

summary.revenue: Total revenues of $177.8 billion, up 7.3% reported, up 5.9% in constant currency (cc). Net sales grew 5.7% (cc).
summary.eps: GAAP EPS of $0.67; Adjusted EPS of $0.66, up 8.2% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: Q2 FY27: net sales (cc) increase 4.0%-5.0%, operating income (cc) increase 7.0%-10.0%, adjusted EPS $0.72-$0.74. Full-year FY27: net sales (cc) increase 3.5%-4.5% (unchanged), adjusted operating income (cc) increase 6.0%-8.0% (unchanged), adjusted EPS $2.75-$2.85 (unchanged). Guidance does not assume any impact from IEEPA tariff refunds.
summary.margin: Gross profit rate +6 bps to 24.3%. Walmart U.S. gross profit rate +29 bps to 27.8%. Adjusted operating expenses as a percentage of net sales deleveraged 23 bps to 21.1%.
key_risks: Higher fuel costs: absorbed approximately $175 million, or about 250 bps of operating income growth, from higher than planned fuel costs in global distribution and fulfillment operations.
If elevated fuel cost environment persists, management expects 'somewhat higher retail price inflation in Q2 and the second half of the year.'
Maximum Fair Pricing legislation in pharmacy created a 100-basis point headwind to Walmart U.S. comp sales.

Consumer pressure: lower-income consumers are 'more budget conscious and perhaps navigating financial distress,' with gallons per fill-up at fuel stations falling below 10 for the first time since 2022.
Tariff uncertainty: guidance does not assume any impact from IEEPA tariff refunds; maximum refunds represent less than half of 1% of US annual sales.
key_opportunities: eCommerce growth: global eCommerce sales grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. delivery growing 45% and 36% of store-fulfilled deliveries in under 3 hours.
Advertising business: global advertising grew 37%, with Walmart U.S. up 36% and marketplace seller ad spend up over 50%.
Marketplace: U.S. marketplace net sales grew nearly 50%, with cross-border expansion into Canada and Mexico showing early positive results.
Membership fee revenue: grew 17.4% globally, with Walmart+ net adds reaching a new Q1 high and Sam's Club membership revenue up 5.6%.

General merchandise share gains: highest level in five years, with fashion as a standout and merchandise category mix contributing favorably to Walmart U.S. gross margin for the first time in 18 quarters.

AI and automation: Sparky AI shopping agent weekly active users up over 100% in the quarter; automation scaling across supply chain (50% of eCommerce FC volume automated, 60% of stores receiving freight from automated DCs).

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management uses language such as 'our business is strong,' 'we have momentum and a clear strategy,' and 'we are probably as excited about the potential of our business today than at any point in time in the last few years,' while reiterating full-year guidance despite acknowledged headwinds.
